Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 21, verses 1–6:

Explanation of the words:

"Iqtaraba li-n-nasi hisabuhum" (their reckoning has drawn near to people): i.e., the time of their reckoning has come close, and that is the Day of Resurrection.

"Wa-hum fi ghaflah" (while they are heedless): i.e., heedless of what they are going to face.

"Mu'ridun" (turning away): i.e., turning away from preparing for the Day of Reckoning with righteous deeds, after abandoning shirk and sins.

"Min dhikrin min rabbihim muhdath" (any reminder from their Lord, newly revealed): i.e., any Qur'an sent down from their Lord, freshly revealed.

"Wa-hum yal'abun" (while they play): i.e., mocking and ridiculing.

"Lahiyatan qulubuhum" (their hearts distracted): i.e., preoccupied, diverted from it by what does not benefit, by falsehood, evil and corruption.

"Wa-asarru an-najwa" (and they secretly conferred): i.e., they concealed their private consultation among themselves.

"Adghathu ahlam" (confused dreams): i.e., jumbled visions seen in a dream.

"Bal iftarahu" (rather, he invented it): i.e., he fabricated it and lied, and it was not revealed to him.

"A-fahum yu'minun" (will they then believe?): i.e., they do not believe; the interrogative is for negation.

Meaning of the verses:

He, the Exalted, says, and His word is the truth: ﴿The reckoning of people has drawn near﴾, i.e., the time of their reckoning for their deeds, good and bad, has approached and come close. ﴿While they are heedless﴾ of the reckoning and recompense awaiting them, ﴿turning away﴾ from what they are called to, namely preparing for the Day of Reckoning by abandoning shirk and sins and equipping themselves with faith and righteous deeds. And His saying: ﴿No reminder comes to them from their Lord, newly revealed﴾, i.e., whatever Qur'an God sends down to admonish them and remind them of what it contains, ﴿but they listen to it while they play﴾, i.e., they listen while mocking, scoffing and jesting, not reflecting upon it or pondering over it. And His saying: ﴿Their hearts distracted﴾, i.e., preoccupied and diverted from it, turned away from the guidance and light that the newly revealed verses carry. ﴿And they secretly conferred, those who did wrong﴾, namely the polytheists, who said in their private consultations among themselves: ﴿Is this not but a human like yourselves?﴾, i.e., Muhammad is only a man like you, so how can you believe in him and follow what he brings? He is nothing but a sorcerer. ﴿Will you then approach magic while you see?﴾ What is wrong with you? Where have your minds gone?

God said to His Messenger: ﴿My Lord knows every word in the heavens and the earth, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing﴾, i.e., He hears the words of His servants and knows their deeds. So He, the Exalted, hears what you say of lies and knows my truthfulness and the reality of what I call you to.

And His saying: ﴿Rather, they say﴾, i.e., those conspiring wrongdoers, ﴿"Confused dreams"﴾, i.e., they said about the Qur'an, which comes to them from their Lord newly revealed so that they may be guided by it, that it is jumbled visions of dreams and not the speech of God and His revelation. ﴿Rather, he has invented it﴾: they moved from one saying to another because of their bewilderment. ﴿Rather, he is a poet﴾, i.e., ﷺ, and what he says is not of the kind of poetry that mentions things having no reality or truth. 3. A statement of the bewilderment of the polytheists in the face of the divine revelation and the Prophet ﷺ.

4. Miracles were never a cause of people's guidance; rather they were the cause of their destruction, because this is human nature: when a person does not desire faith and guidance, he will not be guided even if every sign comes to him.

Explanation of the Words:

Wa kam qaṣamnā (وكم قصمنا): That is, and how many of the people of the towns We have destroyed by annihilating them and shattering their bodies.

Kānat ẓālima (كانت ظالمة): That is, its people were wrongdoers.

Yarkuḍūn (يركضون): That is, fleeing and running away.

Ilā mā ut'rafttum fīh (إلى ما أترفتم فيه): That is, [the abundance] of plentiful food, drink, dwellings and mounts.

Tus'alūn (تسألون): That is, you will be questioned about something of your worldly life, as is your custom.

Tilka da'wāhum (تلك دعواهم): That is, their call which they kept repeating, which was: ﴿Woe to us! Indeed we have been wrongdoers.﴾

Ḥaṣīdan khāmidīn (حصيداً خامدين): That is, none of them remained standing; they were like a harvested crop, extinguished, without movement, like a fire when it is put out.

The Meaning of the Verses:

Exalted is He says, warning the Quraysh that what befell others who persisted in denial and obstinacy shall befall them: ﴿And how many a town have We shattered﴾, that is, destroyed and wiped out completely, ﴿a town﴾, that is, the people of a town, ﴿whose people were wrongdoers﴾, that is, its people were wrongdoers through polytheism, sins, arrogance and obstinacy, ﴿and We brought into being after them another people﴾, who were better than those who perished. As for His saying: ﴿So when they perceived Our might, behold, they fled from it﴾, that is, when those wrongdoers ﴿perceived Our might﴾, that is, felt it and realized it with their senses, their hearing and their sight, ﴿behold, they fled from it﴾, from that town, running away in flight from death. The angels will say to them in rebuke and reproach: Do not run away fleeing, ﴿but return to that in which you were made affluent﴾, that is, in which you were blessed with abundant food, drink, clothing, dwelling and mounts, ﴿and to your dwellings, that you may be questioned﴾, as is your custom, about something of your affairs and the affairs of your worldly life. Their answer was what Exalted is He reported about them: ﴿They said: "Woe to us! Indeed we have been wrongdoers."﴾, that is, O our destruction, come, this is your time to come; indeed we have been wrongdoers to ourselves through polytheism, sins, denial and obstinacy. Exalted is He said: ﴿And that call of theirs did not cease until We made them as a harvested field, extinguished﴾, that is, uprooted from their roots, fallen to the ground, extinguished, without movement, like a fire when it is put out so that no flame remains.

Guidance from the Verses:

1- Condemnation of wrongdoing, the highest degree of which is polytheism against God.

2- It is permissible to mock the wrongdoing polytheist when punishment befalls him, as rebuke and reproach.

3- Repentance does not benefit those who are destroyed when they witness the punishment, even if they seek it.

4- The intensity of terror and the sight of punishment may deprive its beholder of his sound judgment, so he babbles and does not know what he is saying.

Kānat ẓālima (كانت ظالمة): That is, its people were wrongdoers.

Yarkuḍūn (يركضون): That is, fleeing and running away.

Ilā mā ut'rafttum fīh (إلى ما أترفتم فيه): That is, [the abundance] of plentiful food, drink, dwellings and mounts.

Tus'alūn (تسألون): That is, you will be questioned about something of your worldly life, as is your custom.

Tilka da'wāhum (تلك دعواهم): That is, their call which they kept repeating, which was: ﴿Woe to us! Indeed we have been wrongdoers.﴾

*Min ladunnā* (from Us): that is, from among what is with Us, of the wide-eyed maidens (ḥūr 'īn) or the angels.

*Bal naqdhifu bi'l-ḥaqq* (Nay, We hurl the truth): that is, We hurl the truth against falsehood.

*Fa-yadmaghuhu* (so it crushes it): that is, it splits its head until the wound reaches its brain and it perishes.

*Fa-idhā huwa zāhiq* (then it is vanishing): that is, departing and dissolving.

*Wa lakumu'l-waylu mimmā taṣifūn* (Woe to you for what you describe): that is, for you is a severe punishment because of your false description of the All-Merciful as having a wife and a son, and of the Messenger as a sorcerer and a fabricator.

*Wa lā yastaḥsirūn* (and they do not tire): that is, they do not grow weary or fatigued so that they abandon glorifying (tasbīḥ).

*Lā yafturūn* (they do not slacken): from glorifying, for it is for them like breath is for us; none of us tires from breathing, and nothing distracts him from it.

The meaning of the verses:

God's destruction of the wrongdoing nations for their polytheism and sins is evidence that He did not create man and life in play and vanity; rather, He created man and life so that He may be remembered and thanked. Whoever turns away from His remembrance and abandons His gratitude, He makes him taste his evil in this world and the Hereafter. This is what the preceding verse indicated and what this verse affirmed, namely His saying: ﴿And We did not create the heaven and the earth and what is between them in play.﴾ That is, not as frivolous beings with no good purpose for Us; rather, We created them with truth, which is the obligation of worshipping Us with remembrance and gratitude to Us. And His saying: ﴿Had We wished to take a pastime﴾ — that is, a companion or a son — as the deniers among the Arabs say, claiming that God became related by marriage to the jinn and so begot the angels, and as the misguided Christians say, that God took Mary as a wife and she bore Him Jesus the Son — exalted is God above what they fabricate. So He refuted this falsehood with reasoned speech, saying: if We had wished to take a pastime to amuse Ourselves, a companion and a son, We would have taken it from among what is with Us, of the wide-eyed maidens and the angels; but We did not wish that, and it is not fitting for Us. Indeed We own everyone in the heavens and on the earth as slaves to Us. How, then, is it conceivable that a slave of Ours be taken as a son, and a female slave as a wife? Even weak, poor people do not permit this: a man does not make his female slave his wife, nor his slave his son, under any circumstances.

And His saying: ﴿Nay, We hurl the truth against falsehood, and it crushes it, and behold, it vanishes﴾ — those vain falsehoods and nonsense are struck by the proofs of the Qur'an, which crush them so that they depart and dissolve, leaving nothing of them. ﴿And woe to you﴾, O liars, ﴿for what you describe﴾ — God as having a wife, a son, and a partner, and the Messenger as a sorcerer, a poet, and a soothsayer, and as a liar. And His saying: ﴿To Him belongs whoever is in the heavens and the earth﴾ — another proof against the claim that He has a wife and a son, for He who owns whoever is in the heavens and the earth is free of need for a companion or a son, since all belong to Him in ownership and disposal.

And His saying: ﴿And those who are with Him do not disdain His worship, nor do they tire﴾ — another proof: ﴿They glorify Him night and day; they do not slacken.﴾ That is, how could He need a wife and a son, when those with Him, the angels, who cannot be counted, worship Him, do not disdain His worship, do not grow bored of it, and do not tire of performing it? 2. The proofs of the Qur'an are the truth; when falsehood is struck with them, they crush it, and it departs and dissolves.

4. Clarification of God's absolute independence from all His creatures.

5. Clarification of the state of the angels in their worship and glorification of God, exalted is He.

**Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on Surah 21, verses 26–29**

**Explanation of the words:**

*Waladan* (a son): That is, among the angels, since they said the angels are the daughters of God. Exalted is God far above that, to a great exaltation.

*Subhanahu* (Glory be to Him): A declaration of His transcendence above taking a son.

*Bal 'ibadun mukramun* (Rather, they are honored servants): They are the angels. Whoever is a servant cannot be a son or a daughter.

*La yasbiquunahu bil-qawl* (They do not speak before Him): That is, they do not speak until He speaks. This is the condition of a servant, who does not precede his master in anything.

*Wa hum bi-amrihi ya'malun* (And they act by His command): That is, they are obedient and well-mannered; they do not act except by His permission.

*Wa la yashfa'una illa liman irtada* (And they do not intercede except for one whom He approves): That is, except for one for whom God has approved intercession.

*Mushfiqun* (fearful): That is, afraid.

*Min dunihi* (besides Him): That is, besides God, such as Iblis, upon him be the curses of God.

*Kadhalika najzi al-zalimin* (Thus We recompense the wrongdoers): That is, those who wrong themselves through polytheism and sins.

**Meaning of the verses:**

After the preceding verses had nullified polytheism and condemned the polytheists, these verses came to nullify another falsehood of the polytheists, namely their attribution of a son to God, Exalted is He. *Fijājan subulan* (wide roads, paths): broad roads they travel, which bring them to wherever they wish to go.

*La'allahum yahtadūn* (so that they may be guided): to their destinations on their journeys.

**The Meaning of the Verses:**

The noble context continues to establish *tawḥīd* (the oneness of God) and the obligation to declare God free of all attributes of deficiency and incapacity. God says: ﴿Have not those who disbelieved seen﴾, that is, the disbelievers in God's oneness, His power, His knowledge, and the obligation to worship Him, [seen] the manifestations of His power, knowledge and wisdom in these created things, the higher and the lower? The heavens and the earth were one mass of primordial mist (*sadīm*), and God created from it the heavens and the earths. Just as the sky is split open by His permission to release rain, the earth is split open to bring forth plants of varied colours, scents, tastes and benefits, and every living thing on this earth, whether human, animal or plant, is made from water. Are not all of these indications of God's existence and of the obligation to worship Him and to affirm His oneness?

So why do people not believe? This is what is indicated by His words in the first verse [30]: ﴿Have not those who disbelieved seen that the heavens and the earth were a joined mass, and We parted them, and made from water every living thing? Will they not then believe?﴾ And His words: ﴿And We placed in the earth firm mountains﴾, that is, fixed mountains, ﴿lest it shake with its inhabitants﴾, that is, lest it move and be agitated with those who dwell on it. ﴿And We made in it﴾, that is, in the earth, ﴿wide roads﴾, that is, open paths for travel upon it, ﴿so that they may be guided﴾, that is, so that they may find their way to their destinations on their journeys. His words: ﴿And We made the sky a protected ceiling﴾, protected from falling and from the devils. His words: ﴿And they, from its signs﴾, from the sun, the moon, the night and the day, since these are signs established within them, ﴿turn away﴾, that is, they do not reflect upon them so as to be guided to knowledge of the Truth, the Mighty and Majestic, and to knowledge of what is due to Him of worship and of *tawḥīd*. His words: ﴿And it is He who created the night and the day, and the sun and the moon; each in an orbit they swim﴾, that is, each of the sun and the moon swims in its own orbit throughout all time. The *falak* is an expression for a circle like the whorl of a spindle, in which a celestial body, whether sun, moon or star, revolves and swims, and does not leave it; for were it to leave, total destruction would befall all the worlds. Glory be to the All-Knowing, the All-Wise. All of these are manifestations of divine power, knowledge and wisdom, which necessitate *tawḥīd* and establish it. But the polytheists turn away from them; they do not reflect, and they are not guided.

From the guidance of these verses:

1. The explanation of the manifestations of God's power, knowledge and wisdom, which necessitate His oneness, belief in Him and obedience to Him.

2. The explanation of the wisdom behind creating the firm mountains.

3. The explanation of the precision of the divine order, and of the greatness of God's knowledge and wisdom, glory be to Him, the Exalted.

4. The turning away of most people from God's signs in the horizons, like their turning away from His Qur'anic signs, is the cause of their ignorance, polytheism, evil and corruption.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 21, verse 39–43:

Explanation of the words:

La yakuffuna (they cannot ward off): That is, they will not be able to prevent or repel the Fire from their faces.

Bal ta'tihim baghtatan (rather it will come upon them suddenly): That is, the Resurrection will come upon them unexpectedly, all of a sudden.

Fatabhatuhum (so it will bewilder them): That is, it will confound them.

Wa la hum yunzarun (nor will they be given respite): That is, they will not be granted time to repent.

Wa haqa bihim (and there will befall them): That is, the punishment at which they used to mock descended upon them.

Man yakla'ukum (who will protect you): That is, who will guard and watch over you.

Min al-Rahman (from the Most Merciful): That is, from His punishment, if He wills to send it down upon you.

Bal hum 'an dhikri rabbihim mu'ridun (rather they turn away from the remembrance of their Lord): That is, they turn away from the Qur'an, so they do not listen to it nor reflect upon it.

Wa la hum minna yusahabun (nor will they find companionship from Us): That is, they will not find anyone who can grant them protection from Our punishment.

Meaning of the verses:

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿If only those who disbelieved would know﴾, those who hastened the punishment and demanded it, at the time when they will be cast into Hell with the Fire consuming their faces and their backs, and they will be unable to protect themselves from it, nor will they be helped by anyone to repel the punishment from them. Had they known this and been certain of it, they would not have demanded the punishment nor hastened its day, which is the Day of Resurrection. This is what is indicated by the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿If only those who disbelieved would know the time when they will not be able to ward off the Fire from their faces, nor from their backs, nor will they be helped﴾, and His saying: ﴿Rather, it will come upon them suddenly and bewilder them, and they will not be able to avert it, nor will they be given respite﴾. That is, the Resurrection will not come upon them with their knowledge of its time and hour, so that they could repent in that case; rather, it will come upon them ﴿suddenly﴾, that is, unexpectedly, ﴿bewildering them﴾, that is, confounding them, ﴿so they will not be able to avert it, nor will they be given respite﴾, that is, they will not be granted time to repent from shirk and sins so that they might be saved from the punishment of the Fire. And His saying: ﴿And messengers were certainly mocked before you, but there befell those who ridiculed them what they had been mocking﴾, which refers to the punishment. This statement is addressed to the Messenger ﷺ as consolation and solace, so that he may be patient over the mockery of Quraysh toward him and their hastening of the punishment, since the like of this happened to the messengers before him, and they remained patient until the punishment descended upon those who mocked the messengers, peace be upon them.

And His saying: ﴿Say: Who protects you by night and by day from the Most Merciful?﴾ Allah the Exalted commands His Messenger to say to those who demand the punishment and hasten it: ﴿Who protects you by night and by day﴾, that is, who will protect you from the Most Merciful if He wills to punish you? No one is able to do that. So why do you not repent to Him through faith, monotheism and obedience to Him and to His Messenger? And His saying: ﴿Rather, they turn away from the remembrance of their Lord﴾: the reason for their not responding to the truth is their turning away from the noble Qur'an, and their not contemplating its verses and not understanding its meanings. And His saying: ﴿Or do they have gods that protect them from Us?﴾ Allah the Exalted denies that the polytheists have gods that could protect them from the punishment of Allah when it descends upon them, and affirms that their gods cannot help them ﴿nor will they be companioned by Us﴾, that is, there is no one to grant them protection from the punishment of Allah, neither from their gods nor from others, so no one can protect them from the punishment of Allah when it befalls them.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of the verses:

1- Affirmation that the Hour will come only suddenly.

2- Affirmation of the doctrine of resurrection and recompense.

3- Consolation of the Messenger ﷺ with what the messengers before him experienced and what they encountered from their peoples.

4- Clarification of the powerlessness of the polytheists' gods to help them by repelling the punishment when it descends upon them.

5- Clarification that the reason for the polytheists' persistence in shirk and disbelief is their unwillingness to reflect upon the noble Qur'an and to contemplate its verses and what they carry of guidance and light.

Wa la hum yunzarun (nor will they be given respite): That is, they will not be granted time to repent.

Wa haqa bihim (and there will befall them): That is, the punishment at which they used to mock descended upon them.

Man yakla'ukum (who will protect you): That is, who will guard and watch over you.

Min al-Rahman (from the Most Merciful): That is, from His punishment, if He wills to send it down upon you.

Bal hum 'an dhikri rabbihim mu'ridun (rather they turn away from the remembrance of their Lord): That is, they turn away from the Qur'an, so they do not listen to it nor reflect upon it.

Meaning of the verses:

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿If only those who disbelieved would know﴾, those who hastened the punishment and demanded it, at the time when they will be cast into Hell with the Fire consuming their faces and their backs, and they will be unable to protect themselves from it, nor will they be helped by anyone to repel the punishment from them. Had they known this and been certain of it, they would not have demanded the punishment nor hastened its day, which is the Day of Resurrection. This is what is indicated by the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿If only those who disbelieved would know the time when they will not be able to ward off the Fire from their faces, nor from their backs, nor will they be helped﴾, and His saying: ﴿Rather, it will come upon them suddenly and bewilder them, and they will not be able to avert it, nor will they be given respite﴾. Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 21, verses 44–47:

Explanation of the words:

*Matta'na ha'ulaa'i wa-aba'ahum* (We gave enjoyment to these and their fathers): that is, with the blessings We bestowed upon them.

*Hatta tala 'alayhimu al-'umr* (until the life grew long for them): so they were deceived by that.

*Nanqusuha min atrafiha* (We reduce it from its edges): that is, by granting victory to the Prophet ﷺ and his companion believers.

*Innama undhirukum bil-wahy* (I only warn you by revelation): that is, by the reports of God Most High which He reveals to me, and there is nothing from me in it.

*Nafkha* (a breath): that is, a light stroke of punishment.

*Ya waylana inna kunna zalimin* (Woe to us, indeed we were wrongdoers): that is, they say, "Woe to us," meaning, "Our destruction!"

*Inna kunna zalimin* (indeed we were wrongdoers): that is, by associating partners with God and denying the Messenger ﷺ.

*Al-mawazin al-qist* (the scales of justice): that is, the just ones.

*Fa-la tuzlamu nafsun shay'an* (so no soul will be wronged in anything): neither by diminishing a good deed nor by increasing an evil deed.

*Mithqala habbah* (the weight of a grain): that is, the weight of a mustard seed.

*Wa-kafa bina hasibin* (and sufficient are We as reckoners): that is, Ones who take account of everything.

Meaning of the verses:

The context continues to refute the claims of the polytheists, so God Most High says: ﴿Nay, We gave enjoyment to these and their fathers﴾ with the blessings We bestowed upon them and upon their fathers, so they thought their gods were the ones protecting them. Rather, God is the Protector, until the life grew long for them, so they were deceived by that. ﴿Do they not see that We come to the land﴾, the land of the Arabian Peninsula, their country, ﴿reducing it from its edges﴾ by the entry of its people into Islam, city after city. ﴿Are they then the victorious?﴾ God is the Victor, for He established His Messenger and the believers and granted them victory. Then He commanded His Messenger to say to them: "O deniers, I only warn you of the punishment, and I make you fear the consequence of your polytheism, by the divine revelation, not from my own accord." And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And the deaf do not hear the call when they are warned﴾. The deaf, because of their love of the falsehood they are upon, do not hear the call when they are warned. In a report it is said: "Your love of a thing makes you blind and deaf." Their love of polytheism and its gods made them unable to hear, so their warning and its absence became equal. And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And if a breath of the punishment of your Lord touches them﴾, that is, a light stroke of punishment, they would surely cry out calling for woe upon themselves, saying ﴿Woe to us! Indeed we were wrongdoers﴾. How then will it be with them when the just scales are set up on the Day of Resurrection, when no soul will be wronged in anything, however small? Even if it be the weight of a grain of a mustard seed of good or evil, We will bring it and weigh it. ﴿And sufficient are We as reckoners﴾, that is, Ones who count the deeds of the servants, by our all-encompassing knowledge of everything and our power which nothing can overcome. Then, O intelligent ones, let us fear God!

Guidance from the verses:

1- A long life and abundant provision often cause pride in their possessor.

2- Love of a thing blinds its lover so that he sees only what he loves, and deafens him so that he hears only what he loves.

3- Demonstration of human weakness: even the least punishment that descends upon him he cannot bear, and he cries out calling, "Woe to us!"

4- Affirmation of the Resurrection, the reckoning, and the recompense.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 21, verses 44–47:

Explanation of the words:

*Matta'na ha'ulaa'i wa-aba'ahum* (We gave enjoyment to these and their fathers): that is, with the blessings We bestowed upon them.

*Hatta tala 'alayhimu al-'umr* (until the life grew long for them): so they were deceived by that.

*Nanqusuha min atrafiha* (We reduce it from its edges): that is, by granting victory to the Prophet ﷺ and his companion believers.

*Innama undhirukum bil-wahy* (I only warn you by revelation): that is, by the reports of God Most High which He reveals to me, and there is nothing from me in it.

*Nafkha* (a breath): that is, a light stroke of punishment.

*Ya waylana inna kunna zalimin* (Woe to us, indeed we were wrongdoers): that is, they say, "Woe to us," meaning, "Our destruction!"

*Inna kunna zalimin* (indeed we were wrongdoers): that is, by associating partners with God and denying the Messenger ﷺ.

*Al-mawazin al-qist* (the scales of justice): that is, the just ones.

*Fa-la tuzlamu nafsun shay'an* (so no soul will be wronged in anything): neither by diminishing a good deed nor by increasing an evil deed.

*Mithqala habbah* (the weight of a grain): that is, the weight of a mustard seed.

*Wa-kafa bina hasibin* (and sufficient are We as reckoners): that is, Ones who take account of everything.

Meaning of the verses:

The context continues to refute the claims of the polytheists, so God Most High says: ﴿Nay, We gave enjoyment to these and their fathers﴾ with the blessings We bestowed upon them and upon their fathers, so they thought their gods were the ones protecting them. Rather, God is the Protector, until the life grew long for them, so they were deceived by that. ﴿Do they not see that We come to the land﴾, the land of the Arabian Peninsula, their country, ﴿reducing it from its edges﴾ by the entry of its people into Islam, city after city. ﴿Are they then the victorious?﴾ God is the Victor, for He established His Messenger and the believers and granted them victory. Then He commanded His Messenger to say to them: "O deniers, I only warn you of the punishment, and I make you fear the consequence of your polytheism, by the divine revelation, not from my own accord." And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And the deaf do not hear the call when they are warned﴾. The deaf, because of their love of the falsehood they are upon, do not hear the call when they are warned. In a report it is said: "Your love of a thing makes you blind and deaf." Their love of polytheism and its gods made them unable to hear, so their warning and its absence became equal. 4- Affirmation of the Resurrection, the reckoning, and the recompense.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 21, verses 48–50:

Explanation of the words:

Al-Furqan: the Torah, because it distinguishes between truth and falsehood, just as the Qur'an does.

Wa diya': that is, it guides to the truth in belief and in law.

Wa dhikran: that is, admonition.

Yakhshawna rabbahum bil-ghayb: that is, they fear their Lord while they have not seen Him in this world, so they do not disobey Him by abandoning an obligation or committing a forbidden act.

Wa hum min al-Sa'ah mushfiqun: that is, they are fearful of the terrors of the Day of Resurrection and its punishment.

Wa hadha dhikrun mubarak: that is, the noble Qur'an, whose blessing is attained by its reciter and by one who acts upon it.

Afa-antum lahu munkirun: the interrogative is for rebuke; the Exalted rebukes those who deny that the Qur'an is the Book of God.

Meaning of the verses:

He, the Exalted, informs that He gave Musa and Harun the Furqan, that is, the truth that distinguished the truth of Musa and Harun from the falsehood of Fir'awn, just as He distinguished between monotheism and polytheism on the day of Badr, the Day of the Furqan. He gave them the Torah as a light by which one is guided in knowing what is lawful and unlawful, in the laws and the rulings, and as a dhikr, that is, an admonition for the God-fearing. The God-fearing are described with two attributes: the first is that they fear their Lord, that is, they fear Him in the unseen, that is, while they do not see Him; the second is that they are fearful of the Hour, that is, of what occurs in it of terrors and punishment. His saying, Exalted is He:

﴿And this is a blessed Reminder﴾ refers to the noble Qur'an and describes it as blessed. Its blessing does not cease; everyone who recites it and acts by what is in it is granted its blessing. Reciting a single letter of it earns ten good deeds. Its wonders never end, its secrets cannot be fully grasped, and not all its realities can be uncovered. It is guidance for whoever seeks guidance and a cure for whoever seeks healing. His saying, Exalted is He:

﴿Will you then deny it?﴾ rebukes the Arabs who believed in the Book of the Jews, since they used to ask them about what was in their book, yet disbelieved in the Qur'an, which is their book, in which is their mention and their honour.

Guidance from the verses:

1- Demonstration of Allah's favour upon Musa and his people, and upon Muhammad (ﷺ) and his community, by the sending down of the Torah to Musa and the Qur'an to Muhammad (ﷺ).

2- Explanation of the attributes of the God-fearing, who fear their Lord in the unseen, so they do not disobey Him by abandoning an obligation or committing a forbidden act, and who are always in a state of apprehension and fear of the Day of Resurrection.

3- Praise of the noble Qur'an, since Allah sent it down as blessed.

4- Rebuke and reproach of whoever reflects upon the Qur'an and denies the guidance and light within it.

**Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on Surah 21, verses 51–58:**

**Explanation of the words:**

*Rushdah* (his right guidance): that God guided him to know his Lord, to believe in Him, to obey Him, and to draw near to Him.

*Al-tamathil* (the images): plural of *timthal*, which is a statue made in the likeness of a human being or an animal.

*Allati antum laha 'akifun* (which you are devoted to): that is, devoted to them, constantly attached to them in worship.

*Am anta mina al-la'ibin* (or are you one of the jesters?): that is, the joking ones, those not serious in what they say or do.

*Rabbukum rabb al-samawat* (your Lord, the Lord of the heavens): that is, the One who deserves to be worshipped, the Owner of the heavens and the earth.

*Alladhi fatarahunna* (who created them): that is, who brought them into being, creating them and originating them without any previous pattern.

*La-akidanna asnamakum* (I will surely plot against your idols): that is, I will surely devise a scheme to break your idols and smash them.

*Judhadhan* (in pieces): crumbs and small fragments.

*Illa kabiran lahum* (except a large one of them): except the largest idol of theirs, for he did not break it.

*La'allahum ilayhi yarji'un* (so that they may turn back to him): so that they may return to Him, believing in God and affirming His oneness after the impotence of their gods has become clear to them.

**The meaning of the verses:**

Continuing the mention of what the Exalted granted to Moses, Aaron and Muhammad (ﷺ) by giving them the Torah and the Qur'an, He mentions that He had earlier bestowed favor upon Abraham, granting him his right guidance in his youth, so that he came to know Him, His majesty and His perfection, the obligation to believe in Him and to worship Him alone, and that the worship of anyone other than Him is false. The Exalted said: ﴿And We had already given Abraham his right guidance before, and We were of him well-aware﴾, meaning, We knew his fitness for the call and for carrying it out. ﴿When he said﴾, that is, at the time he said to his father, Azar, and to his people, denouncing their worship of other than God: ﴿What are these images to which you are devoted?﴾, that is, devoted to them and constantly attached to them. They answered him with what the Exalted reported of them in His saying: ﴿They said, "We found our fathers worshipping them."﴾ Thus they declared their ignorance, for they did not mention any proof for the validity or benefit of worshipping them, and they were content with blind imitation (*taqlid*). Their situation in this is the situation of everyone who worships other than God, for he has no proof for the validity of his worship except the imitation of someone he saw worshipping.

Abraham replied to them with what the Exalted reported of him in His saying: ﴿He said, "Indeed you and your fathers have been in clear error,"﴾ that is, those whom you imitated in the worship of idols, ﴿in clear error﴾, that is, departing from the guidance you ought to follow, an error that needs no proof to establish it. They responded to Abraham's words, as the Exalted reported of them: ﴿They said, "Have you brought us the truth, or are you of the jesters?"﴾, that is, regarding what you have said to us, that we and our fathers are in clear error. ﴿Or are you of the jesters?﴾, that is, in your saying what you have said to us, for you are not serious with us; you are merely a jester and nothing more. Abraham answered them with what the Exalted reported of him in His saying: ﴿He said, "Rather, your Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth, who created them, and I am of those who testify to that."﴾ That is, your Lord is not those images; rather, your true Lord, who deserves your worship, is the One who created the heavens and the earth, bringing them into being in a wondrous creation without any previous pattern, and I am among the witnesses that your Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth, since you have no lord but Him and no true god besides Him. ﴿And by God﴾, swearing by Him, the Exalted: ﴿I will surely plot against your idols﴾, that is, I will surely devise a scheme against them and break them ﴿after you have turned away, retreating﴾, that is, after you have gone away from them and left them alone.

And indeed, when they went out to a festival of theirs, spending a day outside the city, he came to those images and broke them, reducing them to scattered pieces here and there, except for one large idol of theirs, which he left alone ﴿so that they might return to him﴾, that is, return to Abraham and worship with him their Lord, glorified and exalted, when it becomes clear to them that worshipping idols is false, because they were unable to defend themselves, so how could they defend others?

**Guidance from the verses:**

1. Manifestations of God's favor and honor toward those among His servants whom He chose.
2. Affirmation of prophethood and of the oneness of God (*tawhid*), and condemnation of polytheism and polytheists.
3. Censure of blind imitation (*taqlid*), and that it is not a proof nor evidence for the imitator regarding what he believes or does.
4. The legitimacy of giving testimony and its excellence in situations where it is rare and needed.
5. Changing evil by the hand for one who is able to do so takes precedence over changing it by the tongue, and combining the two is better.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 21, verses 59–65:

Explanation of the words:

"By our gods" (bi-ālihatinā): that is, by their idols, which they called gods because they worship them and make them divine.

"A youth who mentions them" (fatan yadhkuruhum): that is, with disparagement and belittling.

"In the sight of the people" (ʿalā aʿyun al-nās): that is, openly, so that they can see it with their own eyes.

"They may bear witness" (yashhadūn): that is, against him, that he is the one who broke the gods, and they may witness the punishment We inflict upon him.

"Did you do this?" (a-anta fa'alta hādhā): this is the form of interrogation and questioning.

"Rather, it was done by their chief, this one" (bal fa'alahu kabīruhum hādhā): he pointed with his finger toward the great idol on which he had hung the axe, saying, "Rather, their chief did this," and he used an indirect expression with his finger to avoid lying (tawriya).

"So they turned back to themselves" (fa-raji'ū ilā anfusihim): that is, after reflection and contemplation they judged themselves to be wrongdoers for worshipping that which cannot speak.

"Then they were turned upside down upon their heads" (thumma nukisū ʿalā ruʾūsihim): that is, after acknowledging the truth they returned to upholding falsehood, becoming like one who is overturned, whose head is placed below and whose feet are above.

"These do not speak" (mā hā'ulāʾi yanṭiqūn): so how can you ask us to question them?

Meaning of the verses:

The noble context continues with what passed between Abraham the Friend of God and his people in dialogue about belief. When Abraham seized the opportunity of the people's departure to their festival outside the town, he entered the hall and broke the idols into scattered pieces, and hung the axe on the great idol of their supposed gods, the chief of them, and then left. When evening came and they returned to the town, they went to the supposed gods to take the food placed before them, which they believed would be blessed through their false belief, and found them shattered and broken. They cried out, saying: ﴿Who has done this to our gods? Indeed, he is among the wrongdoers.﴾ Some of them said to one another: ﴿We heard a youth mention them﴾, that is, a young man who speaks of the gods with disparagement and contempt, whose name was Abraham. Thereupon they said: ﴿Then bring him before the eyes of the people﴾ so that we may see him and examine him; if it is established that he is the one, we will punish him and the people will witness his punishment, which will be a deterrent to others. They brought him, peace be upon him, and began to question him, saying what Allah the Exalted related of them: ﴿Did you do this to our gods, O Abraham?﴾ That is, the breaking and smashing. He answered them as Allah the Exalted related of him, saying: ﴿Rather, their chief did this﴾, pointing with his finger to the chief of the gods, by way of indirection (tawriya), ﴿so ask them, if they can speak﴾, as a rebuke and reproach to them. Here they turned back to themselves with blame, saying: ﴿Indeed, you are the wrongdoers﴾, that is, in that you worship what neither speaks nor answers nor defends itself, let alone others. And the saying of the Exalted: ﴿Then they were turned upside down upon their heads﴾ means that Allah overturned them, so that after they recognized the truth and blamed themselves, they returned to disputing with falsehood, saying: ﴿Indeed you know﴾, that is, O Abraham, that ﴿these do not speak﴾, so how can you ask us to question them when you know they do not speak. Their acknowledgment that the supposed gods do not speak was also a reversal on their part, since they admitted the falsehood of those gods.

Guidance from the verses:

1- Injustice is recognized by all people and is condemned among them; had it not been for the darkness of souls, they would not have acknowledged it among themselves.

2- Producing evidence for claims is an established matter in the custom of people, and the revealed laws have brought it before.

3- The method of trial relies first on questioning and interrogation.

4- The permissibility of tawriya (indirect speech) out of fear of uttering a lie.

Explanation of the words:

"By our gods" (bi-ālihatinā): that is, by their idols, which they called gods because they worship them and make them divine.

"A youth who mentions them" (fatan yadhkuruhum): that is, with disparagement and belittling.

"In the sight of the people" (ʿalā aʿyun al-nās): that is, openly, so that they can see it with their own eyes.

"They may bear witness" (yashhadūn): that is, against him, that he is the one who broke the gods, and they may witness the punishment We inflict upon him.

"Did you do this?" (a-anta fa'alta hādhā): this is the form of interrogation and questioning.

"Rather, it was done by their chief, this one" (bal fa'alahu kabīruhum hādhā): he pointed with his finger toward the great idol on which he had hung the axe, saying, "Rather, their chief did this," and he used an indirect expression with his finger to avoid lying (tawriya).

"So they turned back to themselves" (fa-raji'ū ilā anfusihim): that is, after reflection and contemplation they judged themselves to be wrongdoers for worshipping that which cannot speak.

"Then they were turned upside down upon their heads" (thumma nukisū ʿalā ruʾūsihim): that is, after acknowledging the truth they returned to upholding falsehood, becoming like one who is overturned, whose head is placed below and whose feet are above.

"These do not speak" (mā hā'ulāʾi yanṭiqūn): so how can you ask us to question them?

Meaning of the verses:

The noble context continues with what passed between Abraham the Friend of God and his people in dialogue about belief. When Abraham seized the opportunity of the people's departure to their festival outside the town, he entered the hall and broke the idols into scattered pieces, and hung the axe on the great idol of their supposed gods, the chief of them, and then left. When evening came and they returned to the town, they went to the supposed gods to take the food placed before them, which they believed would be blessed through their false belief, and found them shattered and broken. They cried out, saying: ﴿Who has done this to our gods? Indeed, he is among the wrongdoers.﴾ Some of them said to one another: ﴿We heard a youth mention them﴾, that is, a young man who speaks of the gods with disparagement and contempt, whose name was Abraham. Thereupon they said: ﴿Then bring him before the eyes of the people﴾ so that we may see him and examine him; if it is established that he is the one, we will punish him and the people will witness his punishment, which will be a deterrent to others. They brought him, peace be upon him, and began to question him, saying what Allah the Exalted related of them: ﴿Did you do this to our gods, O Abraham?﴾ That is, the breaking and smashing. He answered them as Allah the Exalted related of him, saying: ﴿Rather, their chief did this﴾, pointing with his finger to the chief of the gods, by way of indirection (tawriya), ﴿so ask them, if they can speak﴾, as a rebuke and reproach to them. Here they turned back to themselves with blame, saying: ﴿Indeed, you are the wrongdoers﴾, that is, in that you worship what neither speaks nor answers nor defends itself, let alone others. And the saying of the Exalted: ﴿Then they were turned upside down upon their heads﴾ means that Allah overturned them, so that after they recognized the truth and blamed themselves, they returned to disputing with falsehood, saying: ﴿Indeed you know﴾, that is, O Abraham, that ﴿these do not speak﴾, so how can you ask us to question them when you know they do not speak. Their acknowledgment that the supposed gods do not speak was also a reversal on their part, since they admitted the falsehood of those gods.

Guidance from the verses:

1- Injustice is recognized by all people and is condemned among them; had it not been for the darkness of souls, they would not have acknowledged it among themselves.

2- Producing evidence for claims is an established matter in the custom of people, and the revealed laws have brought it before.

3- The method of trial relies first on questioning and interrogation.

4- The permissibility of tawriya (indirect speech) out of fear of uttering a lie.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 21, verses 66–72:

Explanation of the words:

"ما لا ينفعكم شيئاً" (what neither benefits you at all): i.e., gods that neither benefit you nor harm you if they wish to harm you.

"أفٍ لكم" (Uff to you): i.e., ugliness/disgust for you and for what you worship besides God.

"قالوا: حرقوه" (They said, "Burn him"): i.e., burn him with fire in support of your gods whom he broke.

"برداً وسلاماً" (coolness and safety): i.e., upon Ibrahim, and so it was; nothing was burned of him except his bonds, "the rope with which he was tied."

"كيداً" (a plot): namely, burning him with fire to be rid of him.

"فجعلناهم الأخسرين" (so We made them the greatest losers): in that he came out of the fire and it did not burn him, he escaped their grip, their plot came to nothing, and they gained nothing.

"ونجيناه ولوطاً" (And We delivered him and Lut): i.e., the son of his brother, Haran.

"التي باركنا فيها" (to the land which We have blessed): namely, the land of al-Sham (Greater Syria).

"ويعقوب نافلة" (and Ya'qub as an additional gift): an increase upon his request for a son; he asked for a son, so He gave him what he asked and added another.

"وكلاً جعلنا صالحين" (And We made each of them righteous): i.e., We made each one of them among the righteous who fulfil the rights of God completely and the rights of people likewise.

Meaning of the verses:

He, exalted is He, informs that Ibrahim, peace be upon him, said to his people, rejecting their worship of their gods: "﴿Do you worship besides God that which can neither benefit you at all nor harm you?﴾" i.e., do you worship gods besides God, knowing that they neither benefit you nor harm you, do not speak when asked, and do not answer when questioned? "﴿Uff to you and to what you worship besides God﴾" i.e., ugliness to you and to those images you worship besides God, the Creator, the Provider, the One who harms and benefits. "﴿Will you not then use your reason?﴾" — the ugliness of their worship and the falsehood of deifying them, when they are inanimate objects that neither hear, speak, benefit, nor harm. Here they answered with what He, exalted is He, related about them, and they said: "﴿Burn him﴾" i.e., burn Ibrahim with fire, "﴿and support your gods﴾" which he humiliated and broke, "﴿if you are going to act.﴾" i.e., if you truly and sincerely intend to support them. They carried out what they had agreed upon: they gathered firewood, kindled the fire in a special enclosure, and threw him into it by means of a catapult, because of its intense blaze and fierce heat. God, exalted is He, said to the fire what He related in His words: "﴿We said, 'O fire, be coolness and safety upon Ibrahim!'﴾" So it was as He had asked of it, and it burned nothing of him except his bonds, the rope with which his hands and feet were tied. Had He not said "and safety," it would have been possible for the fire to turn into a mountain of ice, and Ibrahim, peace be upon him, would have perished by it. It is narrated that when the father of Ibrahim saw that the fire had not burned him, while he was sweating profusely, he said: "How excellent a Lord is your Lord, O Ibrahim!" His, exalted is He, words: "﴿They intended a plot against him, but We made them the greatest losers﴾" i.e., they intended a scheme against Ibrahim, namely burning him with fire; God frustrated their endeavour, delivered His servant and close friend from the fire, nullified what they had hoped for, and so they lost in all their deeds by which they intended to destroy Ibrahim. His, exalted is He, words: "﴿And We delivered him and Lut﴾" i.e., We delivered Ibrahim and the son of his brother, Haran, who is Lut, "﴿to the land which We have blessed for all the worlds﴾" namely the land of al-Sham. Ibrahim settled in Palestine, and Lut settled in al-Mu'tafikah, which are the villages of the people of Lut; after their destruction it became a lake unfit for life. His words: "﴿which We have blessed for all the worlds﴾" mean He blessed its provisions with abundant trees, rivers, and fruits for everyone who dwells there among people, whether believer or disbeliever, according to His words: "﴿for all the worlds﴾." His, exalted is He, words: "﴿And We bestowed upon him﴾" i.e., upon Ibrahim, Ishaq, when he asked God for a child, "and Ya'qub as an additional gift." Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 21, verses 73–77:

Explanation of the words:

A'immah (leaders): those who are followed in good.

Yahduna bi-amrina (they guide by Our command): they guide people and teach them what brings them perfection, salvation and happiness, by God's permission granted to them, since He made them messengers conveying His message.

Wa-kanu lana 'abidin (and they were worshipping Us): i.e., humble, obedient, and upholding Our command.

Wa-Lutan atayna-hu hukman wa-'ilman (And Lot—We gave him judgment and knowledge): i.e., We gave Lot hukm (judgment), meaning the ability to decide between disputants, and fiqh (understanding) in religion. All of this falls under prophethood and messengership, and He had made him a prophet and sent him.

Ta'mal al-khaba'ith (doing the vile deeds): such as sodomy and other corruptions.

Fasiqin (wicked): i.e., sinners, rebellious against the Shari'ah, abandoning acting upon it.

Wa-Nuhan idh nada min qabl (And Noah, when he called before): i.e., remember Noah when he supplicated his Lord against his disbelieving people.

Min al-karb al-'azim (from the great distress): i.e., from the drowning caused by the flood that covered the surface of the earth.

Meaning of the verses:

The noble context continues to mention God's favours upon Abraham and his offspring, so He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And We made them﴾, i.e., Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, leaders who guide, to be followed in good, and who guide people to the true religion of God, by God's charge to them to do so, as He made them prophets and sent them. This has the same meaning as His saying: ﴿And We made them leaders guiding by Our command﴾, and His saying: ﴿And We inspired in them the doing of good deeds, the establishment of prayer and the giving of zakat﴾, i.e., We revealed to them that they should do good deeds (khayrat, plural of khayr, which is everything beneficial and not harmful, containing God's good pleasure), and establish prayer and give zakat. His saying: ﴿And they were worshipping Us﴾, i.e., they carried out Our command in what We commanded them, and were obedient to Us, humble. This is praise of them with the most beautiful attributes and the best conditions. His saying: ﴿And Lot—We gave him judgment and knowledge, and We delivered him from the town that was doing the vile deeds. Indeed they were a people of evil, wicked﴾, i.e., just as We gave Abraham and his two sons what We gave them of favour and bounty mentioned in this context, We gave Lot—who had emigrated with his uncle Abraham—also judgment, knowledge, prophethood and messengership, including the goodness of judgment and decision, the secrets of the Shari'ah and understanding of religion. This is one favour; and another is that We delivered him from the town that was doing the vile deeds, and destroyed its people because they were a people of evil who did not produce anything but what harms creatures, wicked against Our command and outside Our obedience. His saying: ﴿And We admitted him into Our mercy; indeed he was among the righteous﴾ is another, greater favour: admitting him into the company of those granted God's special mercy, because he was one of God's righteous servants.

His saying: ﴿And Noah﴾, i.e., remember, O Our Messenger, among these righteous ones, Our servant and messenger Noah, the time when he called upon his Lord before (Abraham), saying: "I am overcome, so help [me]." ﴿So We answered him and saved him and his family from the great distress﴾, for God, the Exalted, saved him and his family except his wife and son Canaan, for they were not of his family because of their disbelief and wrongdoing, and so they were among the drowned. His saying: ﴿And We helped him against the people who denied Our signs﴾, i.e., We helped him by saving him from them, so they did not touch him with harm; and We drowned them all, because they were a people of evil, wicked and wrongdoing.

Guidance of the verses:

1- The excellence of calling to God, and the nobility of those who do it.

2- The excellence of establishing prayer, giving zakat and doing good deeds.

3- God's praise of His friends and righteous servants for their worship and humility before Him.

4- When wickedness spreads among a nation, it deserves destruction and ruin.

5- Condemnation of wickedness and warning against its consequences, for it is destructive, and God forbid.

6- Affirmation and confirmation of Muhammadan prophethood, since such narratives can only come to one who receives revelation.

This is one favour; and another is that We delivered him from the town that was doing the vile deeds, and destroyed its people because they were a people of evil who did not produce anything but what harms creatures, wicked against Our command and outside Our obedience. 2- The excellence of establishing prayer, giving zakat and doing good deeds.

3- God's praise of His friends and righteous servants for their worship and humility before Him.

4- When wickedness spreads among a nation, it deserves destruction and ruin.

5- Condemnation of wickedness and warning against its consequences, for it is destructive, and God forbid.

6- Affirmation and confirmation of Muhammadan prophethood, since such narratives can only come to one who receives revelation.

*We gave understanding of it (fahhamnaha):* that is, the case in which the judgment was passed.

*And to each We gave judgment and knowledge:* that is, to each of Dawud and his son Sulayman We gave judgment, meaning prophethood, and knowledge of the laws of Allah and their understanding (fiqh).

*Glorifying (yusabbihna):* that is, with him when he glorified (Allah).

*And We were ever doers (of it):* that is, for what is stranger and more wondrous than the glorification of the mountains and birds, so do not be amazed.

*A craft of armour for you (sana'at libus lakum):* this is the coats of mail, which are part of war gear.

*To protect you (lituhsinakum):* that is, to shield you and guard you from the strike of swords and the thrust of spears.

*Will you then be grateful? (fahal antum shakirun):* that is, be grateful; the interrogative here carries the meaning of a command.

*To the land which We have blessed (ila al-ardi allati barakna):* that is, the land of al-Sham (Greater Syria).

*Diving (yaghusun):* that is, into the depths of the sea to extract jewels.

*And performing other work (wa ya'maluna 'amalan dun dhalika):* that is, other than diving, such as building and other crafts.

*And We were guardians of them (wa kunna lahum hafizin):* that is, guardians of their works, so that they would not spoil them.

Meaning of the verses:

The noble context continues to mention the bounties of Allah the Exalted and His favour upon whomever He wills of His servants. In this is an affirmation of the prophethood of His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, which Quraysh denied. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And Dawud and Sulayman﴾, that is, and mention, O our Prophet, Dawud and Sulayman, ﴿when they judged concerning the field﴾, that is, recall the time when they were judging the field in which ﴿the flock of certain people grazed﴾, that is, grazed in it at night without a shepherd, so it ate it up and destroyed it, ﴿and We were witnesses to their judgment﴾, present, nothing of what each of them judged being hidden from Us. Dawud judged that the owner of the field should take the flock in compensation for what it destroyed, since the value of the destroyed crop equals the value of the flock that destroyed it. Sulayman judged that the owner of the flock should take the field and tend it until it returns as it was, and the owner of the field should take the flock to benefit from its wool, milk and young; when the field is returned to him as it was, and the flock is returned to its owner with nothing lacking from it, this is the judgment. Allah the Exalted informs that He gave Sulayman understanding of it, and it is more just than the first, which is His saying: ﴿So We gave understanding of it﴾, that is, the judgment, or the case, or the ruling, to Sulayman. He did not rebuke Dawud for his judgment, and said: ﴿And to each We gave judgment and knowledge﴾, to forestall what some may think, that Dawud was lower than his son in knowledge and judgment.

His saying: ﴿And We subjected the mountains to glorify along with Dawud, and the birds﴾. This is a mention of some of the favours bestowed upon Dawud, peace be upon him: that He subjected the mountains and birds to glorify with him when he glorified, whether he commanded them to do so and they obeyed, or he did not command them; for when he prayed and glorified, they prayed and glorified along with him. His saying: ﴿And We were ever doers﴾, that is, of what is more wondrous than subjecting the mountains and birds to glorify with Sulayman, for nothing is beyond Us, and this was written in the Book of Decrees and brought forth in its time. His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And We taught him﴾, that is Dawud, ﴿the craft of armour for you﴾, which are the full coats of mail that protect their wearers from the thrust of spears and the strike of swords by Allah's permission; they are an instrument of war. Therefore the Exalted said: ﴿to protect you from your violence﴾. ﴿Will you then be grateful?﴾ This is a command to His servants to give thanks for His favour upon them. Thanks is given by praising Allah the Exalted, acknowledging His favour, obeying Him, and directing the blessing to the purpose for which He bestowed it upon His servant. His saying: ﴿And to Sulayman﴾, that is, and We subjected to Sulayman ﴿the wind, violent﴾, extremely swift, ﴿running at his command to the land which We have blessed therein﴾, for he would set out to fight at the beginning of the day and at its end the wind would bring him back, carrying his carpet, which is like the largest warship of today, to the land which Allah has blessed, namely the land of al-Sham.

His saying: ﴿And We were, of everything, knowing﴾. The Exalted informs that He was and remains knowing of everything, what appears to people and what is hidden from them; all events in the cosmos occur according to Allah's knowledge, permission, decree and wisdom, and therefore obedience is due to Him and He deserves divinity and worship.

His saying: ﴿And of the devils were those who dived for him﴾, that is, and We subjected to Sulayman some of the devils who dived for him into the depths of the seas to extract jewels, ﴿and they did work other than that﴾, such as building, making images, prayer niches (mahareeb), basins (jifan), and other things. His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And We were guardians of them﴾, that is, and We were guardians of the works of those jinn workers, knowing them, so that they would not spoil them after completing them out of cunning or deceit; it is related that they would work and then spoil what they had made, so that no one would benefit from it.

All of this is from Allah's favour upon Dawud, Sulayman and others, and it is much. So glory be to the Lord of bounties and graces, the God of truth and Lord of the worlds.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1- The obligation to appoint judges to rule among people.

2- The ruling on livestock grazing in people's fields. Although our law differs from the law of those before us, our ruling is: if the livestock graze at night, the owner of the livestock compensates the owner of the crop for the damage; if they graze by day, the owner of the crop has no claim, because he is obliged to guard his crop from the grazing of people's livestock, based on the hadith "The wound caused by an animal is unpunished" and the hadith of al-Bara' ibn 'Azib's she-camel.

3- The virtue of glorification (tasbih).

4- The obligation to make instruments of war and prepare them for jihad in the way of Allah.

5- The obligation to thank Allah for every blessing that comes to the servant.

6- The statement of Allah's subjugation of the jinn to Sulayman, who did things for him.

7- Affirmation of the prophethood of the Messenger ﷺ, for whoever sent these messengers and bestowed upon them what He bestowed cannot be disputed in sending Muhammad as a messenger, since He sent messengers before him.

8- Every event that occurs in the cosmos occurs by Allah's knowledge, His decree, and for a wisdom that requires it.

His saying: ﴿And of the devils were those who dived for him﴾, that is, and We subjected to Sulayman some of the devils who dived for him into the depths of the seas to extract jewels, ﴿and they did work other than that﴾, such as building, making images, prayer niches (mahareeb), basins (jifan), and other things. His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And We were guardians of them﴾, that is, and We were guardians of the works of those jinn workers, knowing them, so that they would not spoil them after completing them out of cunning or deceit; it is related that they would work and then spoil what they had made, so that no one would benefit from it.

All of this is from Allah's favour upon Dawud, Sulayman and others, and it is much. So glory be to the Lord of bounties and graces, the God of truth and Lord of the worlds.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1- The obligation to appoint judges to rule among people.

2- The ruling on livestock grazing in people's fields. Although our law differs from the law of those before us, our ruling is: if the livestock graze at night, the owner of the livestock compensates the owner of the crop for the damage; if they graze by day, the owner of the crop has no claim, because he is obliged to guard his crop from the grazing of people's livestock, based on the hadith "The wound caused by an animal is unpunished" and the hadith of al-Bara' ibn 'Azib's she-camel.

3- The virtue of glorification (tasbih).

4- The obligation to make instruments of war and prepare them for jihad in the way of Allah.

5- The obligation to thank Allah for every blessing that comes to the servant.

6- The statement of Allah's subjugation of the jinn to Sulayman, who did things for him.

7- Affirmation of the prophethood of the Messenger ﷺ, for whoever sent these messengers and bestowed upon them what He bestowed cannot be disputed in sending Muhammad as a messenger, since He sent messengers before him.

8- Every event that occurs in the cosmos occurs by Allah's knowledge, His decree, and for a wisdom that requires it.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 21, verses 78–82:

Explanation of the words:

*In the field (al-harth):* that is, in the vineyard that the livestock grazed at night.

*Grazed in it (nafashat fihi):* that is, they grazed it at night without a shepherd.

*Witnesses (shahidin):* that is, present, so that the issuing of their judgment in the case is not hidden from us; nothing of that is concealed from Us.

*We gave understanding of it (fahhamnaha):* that is, the case in which the judgment was passed.

*And to each We gave judgment and knowledge:* that is, to each of Dawud and his son Sulayman We gave judgment, meaning prophethood, and knowledge of the laws of Allah and their understanding (fiqh).

*Glorifying (yusabbihna):* that is, with him when he glorified (Allah).

*And We were ever doers (of it):* that is, for what is stranger and more wondrous than the glorification of the mountains and birds, so do not be amazed.

*A craft of armour for you (sana'at libus lakum):* this is the coats of mail, which are part of war gear.

*To protect you (lituhsinakum):* that is, to shield you and guard you from the strike of swords and the thrust of spears.

*Will you then be grateful? (fahal antum shakirun):* that is, be grateful; the interrogative here carries the meaning of a command.

*To the land which We have blessed (ila al-ardi allati barakna):* that is, the land of al-Sham (Greater Syria).

*Diving (yaghusun):* that is, into the depths of the sea to extract jewels.

*And performing other work (wa ya'maluna 'amalan dun dhalika):* that is, other than diving, such as building and other crafts.

*And We were guardians of them (wa kunna lahum hafizin):* that is, guardians of their works, so that they would not spoil them.

The noble context continues to mention the bounties of Allah the Exalted and His favour upon whomever He wills of His servants. In this is an affirmation of the prophethood of His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, which Quraysh denied. Dawud judged that the owner of the field should take the flock in compensation for what it destroyed, since the value of the destroyed crop equals the value of the flock that destroyed it. Sulayman judged that the owner of the flock should take the field and tend it until it returns as it was, and the owner of the field should take the flock to benefit from its wool, milk and young; when the field is returned to him as it was, and the flock is returned to its owner with nothing lacking from it, this is the judgment. Allah the Exalted informs that He gave Sulayman understanding of it, and it is more just than the first, which is His saying: ﴿So We gave understanding of it﴾, that is, the judgment, or the case, or the ruling, to Sulayman. His saying: ﴿And to Sulayman﴾, that is, and We subjected to Sulayman ﴿the wind, violent﴾, extremely swift, ﴿running at his command to the land which We have blessed therein﴾, for he would set out to fight at the beginning of the day and at its end the wind would bring him back, carrying his carpet, which is like the largest warship of today, to the land which Allah has blessed, namely the land of al-Sham.

His saying: ﴿And We were, of everything, knowing﴾. The Exalted informs that He was and remains knowing of everything, what appears to people and what is hidden from them; all events in the cosmos occur according to Allah's knowledge, permission, decree and wisdom, and therefore obedience is due to Him and He deserves divinity and worship.

His saying: ﴿And of the devils were those who dived for him﴾, that is, and We subjected to Sulayman some of the devils who dived for him into the depths of the seas to extract jewels, ﴿and they did work other than that﴾, such as building, making images, prayer niches (mahareeb), basins (jifan), and other things. 2- The ruling on livestock grazing in people's fields. Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 21, verses 83–86:

Explanation of the words:

Wa-Ayyub (وأيوب): i.e., and mention Ayyub (Job).

Idh nada rabbahu (إذ نادى ربه): i.e., he called upon his Lord when he was tested with the loss of his wealth and children and the sickness of his body.

Massaniya ad-durr (مسني الضر): this is what harmed his body, his wealth, or his children.

Wa-dhikra lil-'abidin (وذكرى للعابدين): i.e., an admonition for the worshippers, so that they may be patient and be rewarded.

Wa-adkhalnahum fi rahmatina (وأدخلناهم في رحمتنا): by which We made them prophets, so they joined the company of the prophets; "indeed they were among the righteous."

Meaning of the verses:

The noble context continues to mention the bounties of God Most High and His favour upon whomever He wills of His righteous servants. His saying, may He be exalted, in the first verse [83]: ﴿And Job﴾, i.e., mention Our servant in his gratitude, his patience, and his swift return (to Us). We tested him with health, wealth, and children, and he was grateful; then We tested him with sickness, the loss of wealth, family, and children, and he was patient. Mention him ﴿when he called out to his Lord﴾, i.e., supplicating humbly after the trial had reached its limit, "my Lord," meaning, O Lord, ﴿indeed harm has touched me, and You are the Most Merciful of the merciful﴾. ﴿So We answered him﴾ in his supplication ﴿and removed the harm that was upon him, and We gave him his family﴾, meaning wife and children, ﴿and the like of them with them﴾, i.e., He multiplied for him what had been taken from him through the trial, after his patience. As for wealth, the Prophet ﷺ mentioned that there rained down upon him a swarm of golden locusts, and Job began gathering them in his garment eagerly. His Lord asked him about that, and he said: "Who is it that could be independent of Your blessing, O Lord?" His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿a mercy from Us﴾, i.e., We showed him special mercy, and We made his story a reminder and admonition for those who worship Us, for We test them with ease and hardship, so that they may be grateful and patient, emulating Our servant Job. ﴿Indeed We found him patient; an excellent servant; indeed he was ever turning (to Us)﴾ [Sad: 44].

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And Ishmael and Idris and Dhul-Kifl﴾, i.e., mention, among those chosen from the people of patience and gratitude, Ishmael son of Abraham the Friend (Khalil), Idris, who is Enoch, and Dhul-Kifl. ﴿All of them were among the patient﴾ in Our worship, ﴿the grateful for Our blessings﴾. ﴿And We admitted them into Our mercy﴾, so We made prophets of whomever We made prophets among them, and We bestowed favour upon them and honoured them with Our nearness; ﴿indeed they were among the righteous﴾.

Guidance from the verses:

1- The high rank of patience, and likewise gratitude: the former in adversity, the latter in blessings.

2- The virtue of supplication, which is the gate of response; its path is that whoever is inspired to supplicate is inspired to be answered.

3- In the lives of the righteous there are admonitions, and in the stories of earlier people there are lessons.

4- Whoever is tested with the loss of wealth, family, or children and is patient, God will grant him a replacement. What is said at calamity is: "Indeed we belong to God and to Him we return. O God, reward me in my calamity and give me something better in exchange for it."

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 21, verses 87–91:

Explanation of the words:

Dha al-Nun (Dhu'l-Nun): he is Yunus ibn Matta, peace be upon him. He is called "Dhu'l-Nun" (the one of the fish) in reference to al-Nun, which is the fish, in the words of the Most High: ﴿And do not be like the companion of the fish﴾ [al-Qalam: 48], because a large fish swallowed him.

Idh dhahaba mughadiban (when he went off in anger): that is, angry with his Lord, the Most High, when he did not return to his people after learning that Allah had lifted the punishment from them.

Fa-zanna an lan naqdira alayhi (and he thought that We would not decree against him): that is, that We would not confine him and restrict him in the belly of the fish because of his anger.

Fi'l-zulumat (in the darknesses): the darkness of the fish, the darkness of the sea, and the darkness of the night.

Wa najjaynahu min al-ghamm (and We delivered him from the distress): that is, the anguish that befell him while he was in the belly of the fish.

La tadharni fardan (do not leave me alone): that is, without a child who would inherit from me prophethood, knowledge and wisdom, and who would inherit from the family of Ya'qub.

Raghaban wa rahaban (in hope and in fear): that is, desiring what is with Us and fearing what is from Us, meaning in fear and in hope.

Ahsanat farjaha (she guarded her chastity): that is, she protected and preserved it from immorality.

Min ruhina (of Our spirit): that is, Jibril, when he breathed into the front of her garment, peace be upon her.

Ayatan lil-alamin (a sign for the worlds): that is, a sign of Allah's power and of the obligation to worship Him by remembering Him and giving thanks to Him.

Meaning of the verses:

The noble context continues to mention the favour and bounty of Allah, the Most High, upon whomever He wills of His servants. He, the Most High, said: ﴿And Dhu'l-Nun﴾, that is, remember Dhu'l-Nun, namely Yunus ibn Matta, ﴿when he went off in anger﴾ against his Lord, the Most High, because he did not endure remaining with his people, calling them to the Oneness of Allah, worship of Him, obedience to Him and obedience to His Messenger. So he asked for punishment for them. When they repented and the punishment was lifted from them because of their repentance, and he learned of that, he did not return to them. This was his anger at his Lord, the Most High. And His saying about him: ﴿and he thought that We would not decree against him﴾, that is, Yunus, peace be upon him, thought that Allah, the Most High, would not confine him in the belly of the fish or restrict him. This was a good assumption of his about his Lord, glorified and exalted is He. But because of his anger at his Lord by not returning to his people after the punishment had been lifted from them, his Lord afflicted him as a purification for him from the matter of the slight transgression, by casting him into three darknesses: the darkness of the fish, the sea, and the night. Then He inspired him with the supplication by which deliverance comes, and he kept glorifying Allah in the three darknesses: ﴿There is no deity except You; glory be to You; indeed, I have been of the wrongdoers﴾. So Allah the Most High answered him, and this is the meaning of His saying: ﴿And Dhu'l-Nun, when he went off in anger, and thought that We would not decree against him, then called out within the darknesses, "There is no deity except You; glory be to You; indeed I have been of the wrongdoers." So We answered him and delivered him from the distress﴾ which had befallen him from being in the darknesses, imprisoned, with no companion, no food and no drink, together with the anguish of his own soul over not returning to his people, though Allah had saved them from the punishment. This was the cause of the affliction. And His saying: ﴿Thus do We deliver the believers﴾ from the trials that may befall them.

And His saying: ﴿And Zakariyya﴾, that is, remember, O our Messenger, Zakariyya at the time when he called upon his Lord, supplicating humbly and saying: ﴿My Lord﴾, that is, O Lord, ﴿do not leave me alone﴾, that is, do not leave me alone without a child to inherit from me my prophethood, my knowledge and my wisdom, and to inherit that from the family of Ya'qub, so that prophethood and righteousness do not cease among them. And His saying: ﴿and You are the best of inheritors﴾. He mentioned this expression seeking a means of approach to his Lord, so that He would answer his supplication, and He answered him, and praise be to Allah.

So We gave him Yahya, and We made his wife fit for him by making her fertile after having been barren, good in form and in character. And His saying: ﴿Indeed they used to hasten to good deeds﴾, that is, Zakariyya, Yahya and his mother used to hasten to acts of obedience and devotion, that is, to perform them and to be prompt in them.
