Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 21, verses 98–104:

Explanation of the words:

﴿وما تعبدون من دون الله﴾: that is, of idols and images.

﴿حصب جهنم﴾: that is, that with which Hell is kindled.

﴿لو كان هؤلاء آلهة﴾: that is, the idols which the polytheists of Quraysh worship.

﴿ما وردوها﴾: that is, they would have prevented their worshippers from entering the Fire, because they would be gods capable of doing so; but they are not true gods, so they do not prevent their worshippers from entering the Fire.

﴿وكل فيها خالدون﴾: that is, the worshippers among men, and the worshipped among the devils and the idols.

﴿لهم فيها زفير﴾: that is, the people of the Fire have in it groaning and intense breathing, which is the zafir (groaning/sighing).

﴿سبقت لهم منا الحسنى﴾: that is, Allah the Exalted had decreed from eternity that they are people of Paradise.

﴿حسيسها﴾: that is, the sound of its noise.

﴿لا يحزنهم الفزع الأكبر﴾: that is, at the second blast, the blast of resurrection, they will rise from their graves secure and unafraid.

﴿كطي السجل للكتب﴾: that is, the Mighty One, glory be to Him and exalted is He, will fold the heaven as a scroll is folded so that it enters the container.

﴿كما بدأنا أول خلق نعيده﴾: that is, Allah will bring back the creatures as He originated them the first time; people will be raised from their graves barefoot, naked, and uncircumcised, just as they were born, with nothing lacking from them.

Meaning of the verses:

Almighty Allah says to the polytheists with whom the noble surah began, namely the polytheists of Quraysh, warning them: ﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides Allah﴾ of idols and images ﴿are fuel for Hell﴾, meaning you and the idols you worship will be fuel for the Hell which you will inevitably enter. His saying, ﴿Had these been gods, they would not have entered it﴾: had these images of stone which the polytheists worship been true gods, their worshippers would not have entered the Fire, because they would have rescued them from it. Since the polytheists entered it and dwelt in it, this shows that their gods were false gods that deserve no worship in any way. His saying, ﴿And all therein will abide forever﴾: that is, the false objects of worship and their worshippers, all of them, will abide forever in Hell. His saying, ﴿For them therein is groaning, and they therein will not hear﴾: Allah informs that the polytheists in the Fire have groaning, which is intense moaning from the severity of the punishment, and that they will not hear therein because of the abundance of moaning, the intensity of cries, and the horror of the various kinds of punishment. His saying, ﴿Indeed, those for whom the best reward has preceded from Us, they will be removed far from it [Hell]. They will not hear its faintest sound, and they will abide forever in that which their souls desire﴾: this verse was revealed in response to Ibn al-Zib'ara, when he said: if what Muhammad says is true, that we and our gods are in Hell, then the angels are with us in Hell because we worship them, and Jesus and Ezra are in Hell because the Jews worshipped Ezra and the Christians worshipped the Messiah. Allah informed that whoever is worshipped without his consent, and who was devoted to Allah and drew near to Him through acts of obedience, is among those for whom the best reward has preceded from Us, that they are people of Paradise; these are removed far from it, that is, from Hell, ﴿they will not hear its faintest sound﴾, that is, the sound of it, while they are in Paradise and have therein what their souls desire, abiding forever. They will not be grieved by the greatest terror when they rise from their graves; rather, they will be secure. ﴿And the angels will receive them﴾ upon rising from their graves with greeting and congratulation, saying to them: ﴿This is your Day which you were promised.﴾ His saying, ﴿The Day We will fold the heaven﴾: that is, this will be realized for them on the day when the Mighty One, majestic in His majesty, folds the heaven with His right hand ﴿as a scroll is folded for the writings﴾, that is, the page for the books.

That is the Day of Resurrection, when the earth will be changed to other than the earth, and the heavens to other than the heavens. His saying, ﴿As We originated the first creation, We will repeat it﴾: that is, He will restore man as He originated his creation, and people will come out of their graves barefoot, naked, and uncircumcised. His saying, ﴿A promise upon Us; indeed, We are ever doing it﴾: that is, We promised to restore creation after their annihilation and decay as a binding promise; indeed, We are ever doing it, so We have fulfilled what We promised, and indeed, We are capable of that.

Guidance of the verses

From the guidance of the verses:

1- Affirmation of tawhid (the oneness of Allah), prophethood, resurrection, and recompense.

2- Whoever is worshipped besides Allah with His command or His consent will be fuel for Hell along with his worshippers; whoever did not command or consent, will not enter the Fire together with those who worshipped him; rather, the worshipper of Him alone will be in the Fire.

3- Demonstration of the greatness and power of Allah, for He folds the heaven with His right hand, while the earth is in His grip on the Day of Resurrection.

4- The raising of people barefoot, naked, and uncircumcised, with nothing removed from them, and without the foreskin, is the fulfillment of Allah's promise in His saying: ﴿As He originated you, you will return﴾ [al-A'raf: 29]. Glory be to the One, the Subduer, the Mighty, the Majestic.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 21, verses 105–112:

Explanation of the words:

"And We had certainly written in the Zabur": that is, in the books We sent down, such as the scrolls of Ibrahim (Abraham), the Tawrat (Torah), the Injil (Gospel), and the Qur'an.

"After the Reminder": that is, after We had written that in the Reminder, which is the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz).

"That the earth": that is, the land of Paradise.

"My righteous servants": they are the people of faith and righteous deeds from all nations, the followers of the messengers in general.

"Indeed, in this is a message": that is, indeed, in the Qur'an is a message (balagh), meaning sufficiency and a means of reaching Paradise. Whoever believes in it and acts upon what is in it enters Paradise.

"For a people who worship": that is, who obey Allah and His Messenger.

"A mercy to the worlds": that is, to mankind and the jinn. The believers who are God-fearing enter Paradise, and the disbelievers are saved from the annihilating punishment (al-isti'sal wa al-ibadah) that used to befall earlier nations.

"Then will you be Muslims?": that is, submit. The interrogative here carries the sense of a command.

"And I do not know": that is, I do not know.

"A trial for you": that is, a test for you.

"Of what you describe": of the lies, such as that the Prophet is a sorcerer, that Allah has taken a son, and that the Qur'an is poetry.

Meaning of the verses:

He, the Exalted, informs His Messenger and the believers of His noble promise, which He wrote in His scriptures sent down after writing it in the Reminder, which is the book of decrees called the Preserved Tablet: that the land of Paradise will be inherited by His righteous servants. This is what the first verse [21:105] indicates. His saying, Exalted is He: "Indeed, in this is a message for a people who worship," means: in this great Qur'an is a message for those who worship Allah by performing His obligations and avoiding His prohibitions, a sufficiency for reaching their aim, which is the pleasure of Allah and Paradise. His saying: "And We have not sent you, except as a mercy to the worlds," informs that He sent His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ) only as a mercy to the worlds, to mankind and the jinn, believer and disbeliever. The believers, by following him, enter the mercy of Allah, which is Paradise, and the disbelievers are secure from the annihilating punishment and extermination in this world, the punishment that used to descend upon nations and peoples when they denied their messengers.

His saying, Exalted is He: "Say, it is only revealed to me that your God is one God. So will you be Muslims?" He commands His Messenger to say to his people and to those who receive his address: what is revealed to me is that your God is one God, that is, your true object of worship is one, namely Allah, the Exalted, there is none other than Him. "So will you be Muslims?" means: submit your hearts and faces to Him, worship Him, and do not worship anything besides Him. So convey this to them, O our Messenger. "But if they turn away" means: they turn away from this demand and do not accept it. "Then say: I have announced to you" means: I have informed you, "on equal terms" means: I and you are equal in that there is no meeting between us; I am at war with you and you are at war with me. His saying, Exalted is He: "And I do not know whether it is near or far, that which you are promised." That is: say to them, O our Messenger: I do not know whether what you are promised of punishment is near or far. The punishment is certain to occur unless you submit, but I do not know its time. In the verse there is a clear warning and severe threat. His saying: "Indeed, He knows what is spoken openly and He knows what you conceal" means: He knows your open slander against Islam, its Book and its Prophet, as He knows what you conceal in your souls of enmity and hatred toward me and what you hide of grudges. In this is a warning and threat to them, and they deserve it.

His saying: "And I do not know" means: and I do not know "perhaps it" means: the delay of the punishment from you after you deserved it, by your fighting Islam and its Prophet, "is a trial for you" means: a test for you, perhaps you will repent, and the punishment will be lifted from you, or it is an enjoyment for you in life until your terms end, after which you will be punished after your death. This knowledge is with my Lord; He knows it, and with this He commanded me to say it to you. His saying, Exalted is He: "He said: My Lord, judge with truth." In another reading: "Say: My Lord, judge with truth," meaning: the Messenger said, after Allah's command to that, "O Lord, judge between me and my people who deny me and oppose Your call and Your servants who believe, with truth," and that is by granting me victory over them or by sending down Your vengeance upon them. His saying: "And our Lord is the Most Merciful, the One whose help is sought against what you describe" means: our Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, the Most Merciful, is the One sought for help to nullify your falsehood, O polytheists, since you ascribed to Allah a son and partners, and described His Messenger as a sorcerer and a liar.

Guidance of the verses

From the guidance of the verses:

1. The believing God-fearing people, who are the righteous, are the inheritors of Paradise, the abode of lasting bliss.

2. In the Noble Qur'an is sufficient provision for whoever believes in it and acts upon what is in it, by attaining the happiness of the Hereafter that they aspire to.

3. Clarification of the virtue of the Prophet (ﷺ) and his honor with his Lord, in that He made him a mercy to the worlds.

4. The obligation of separation between the people of polytheism and the people of monotheism.

5. The obligation of seeking Allah's help in every hardship and difficulty that the servant faces.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 21, verses 105–112:

Explanation of the words:

"And We had certainly written in the Zabur": that is, in the books We sent down, such as the scrolls of Ibrahim (Abraham), the Tawrat (Torah), the Injil (Gospel), and the Qur'an.

"After the Reminder": that is, after We had written that in the Reminder, which is the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz).

"That the earth": that is, the land of Paradise.

"My righteous servants": they are the people of faith and righteous deeds from all nations, the followers of the messengers in general.

"Indeed, in this is a message": that is, indeed, in the Qur'an is a message (balagh), meaning sufficiency and a means of reaching Paradise. Whoever believes in it and acts upon what is in it enters Paradise.

"For a people who worship": that is, who obey Allah and His Messenger.

"A mercy to the worlds": that is, to mankind and the jinn. The believers who are God-fearing enter Paradise, and the disbelievers are saved from the annihilating punishment (al-isti'sal wa al-ibadah) that used to befall earlier nations.

"Then will you be Muslims?": that is, submit. The interrogative here carries the sense of a command.

"And I do not know": that is, I do not know.

"A trial for you": that is, a test for you.

"Of what you describe": of the lies, such as that the Prophet is a sorcerer, that Allah has taken a son, and that the Qur'an is poetry.

Meaning of the verses:

He, the Exalted, informs His Messenger and the believers of His noble promise, which He wrote in His scriptures sent down after writing it in the Reminder, which is the book of decrees called the Preserved Tablet: that the land of Paradise will be inherited by His righteous servants. This is what the first verse [21:105] indicates. His saying, Exalted is He: "Indeed, in this is a message for a people who worship," means: in this great Qur'an is a message for those who worship Allah by performing His obligations and avoiding His prohibitions, a sufficiency for reaching their aim, which is the pleasure of Allah and Paradise. His saying: "And We have not sent you, except as a mercy to the worlds," informs that He sent His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ) only as a mercy to the worlds, to mankind and the jinn, believer and disbeliever. The believers, by following him, enter the mercy of Allah, which is Paradise, and the disbelievers are secure from the annihilating punishment and extermination in this world, the punishment that used to descend upon nations and peoples when they denied their messengers.

His saying, Exalted is He: "Say, it is only revealed to me that your God is one God. So will you be Muslims?" He commands His Messenger to say to his people and to those who receive his address: what is revealed to me is that your God is one God, that is, your true object of worship is one, namely Allah, the Exalted, there is none other than Him. "So will you be Muslims?" means: submit your hearts and faces to Him, worship Him, and do not worship anything besides Him. So convey this to them, O our Messenger. "But if they turn away" means: they turn away from this demand and do not accept it. "Then say: I have announced to you" means: I have informed you, "on equal terms" means: I and you are equal in that there is no meeting between us; I am at war with you and you are at war with me. His saying, Exalted is He: "And I do not know whether it is near or far, that which you are promised." That is: say to them, O our Messenger: I do not know whether what you are promised of punishment is near or far. The punishment is certain to occur unless you submit, but I do not know its time. In the verse there is a clear warning and severe threat. His saying: "Indeed, He knows what is spoken openly and He knows what you conceal" means: He knows your open slander against Islam, its Book and its Prophet, as He knows what you conceal in your souls of enmity and hatred toward me and what you hide of grudges. In this is a warning and threat to them, and they deserve it.

His saying: "And I do not know" means: and I do not know "perhaps it" means: the delay of the punishment from you after you deserved it, by your fighting Islam and its Prophet, "is a trial for you" means: a test for you, perhaps you will repent, and the punishment will be lifted from you, or it is an enjoyment for you in life until your terms end, after which you will be punished after your death. This knowledge is with my Lord; He knows it, and with this He commanded me to say it to you. His saying, Exalted is He: "He said: My Lord, judge with truth." In another reading: "Say: My Lord, judge with truth," meaning: the Messenger said, after Allah's command to that, "O Lord, judge between me and my people who deny me and oppose Your call and Your servants who believe, with truth," and that is by granting me victory over them or by sending down Your vengeance upon them. His saying: "And our Lord is the Most Merciful, the One whose help is sought against what you describe" means: our Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, the Most Merciful, is the One sought for help to nullify your falsehood, O polytheists, since you ascribed to Allah a son and partners, and described His Messenger as a sorcerer and a liar.

Guidance of the verses

From the guidance of the verses:

1. The believing God-fearing people, who are the righteous, are the inheritors of Paradise, the abode of lasting bliss.

2. In the Noble Qur'an is sufficient provision for whoever believes in it and acts upon what is in it, by attaining the happiness of the Hereafter that they aspire to.

3. Clarification of the virtue of the Prophet (ﷺ) and his honor with his Lord, in that He made him a mercy to the worlds.

4. The obligation of separation between the people of polytheism and the people of monotheism.

5. The obligation of seeking Allah's help in every hardship and difficulty that the servant faces.
